content.comment_body: Hello everyone, I'm having trouble getting the week clock settings to work through the web interface. cam 1 and 2 do not function as expected. Clicking on a day doesn't toggle it on or off. However, cam 3 appears to work properly. I've checked all the mappings and the tag table but can't identify any errors. I've attached both the logic and web configuration files. Another issue I'd like resolved is ensuring variable values remain persistent after uploading a new [product_name] program. They are retained after a power cycle but revert to the values in the program blocks after uploading changes. Additionally, the clock at the top right of the 'programma' page does not display the current date/time, although it works fine on the homepage. The webserver responds slowly, especially when navigating between pages. Is this typical, or can it be optimized? Thanks for your attention.
That behavior is expected and is not changeable. I will review your issues with the LSC file and the LWE project later.
You posted a similar question previously regarding this type of program. And you observed that the issue depends on the web browser used. weekly timers on webgui
I tested your uploaded files and everything works properly for me. Testing was done using Firefox. Date and time display operates correctly as well.
Thanks! You are correct, my apologies—I'd set the project aside and forgot about the browser-related aspect.

analysis.insight_summary: The user encountered usability challenges with configuring the week clock via the web interface on a [company_name] device, such as non-responsive controls, variable persistence issues after program updates, and slow webserver performance. Some interface problems were identified as being browser-dependent. Inconsistencies were also noted with date/time display between pages. Another community member confirmed that functionality worked when tested in Firefox.
analysis.user_expectations: The user seeks reliable, browser-independent operation of the week clock controls, maintenance of variable values after program uploads, consistent and accurate date/time display across web pages, and better webserver responsiveness.
